svg.title: country road
svg.desc:
The tab icon.
What was here was `create-vite`'s lightning bolt -- 48 by 46, twenty-two blurred ellipses behind an alpha mask, purple and cyan -- which for sixteen iterations advertised the build tool.
Everything below is drawn from `src/core/palette.js` rather than picked: skyTop #3f82c9, leafMid #5c7f42 for the far hills, grass #7d9450, road #585b66, lineWhite #eceade. The palette is narrow on purpose and an icon is the narrowest place it will ever be used.
Designed for the size it is actually seen at, which is 16 px in a tab: five flat shapes, no gradients, no blur, no filters, and two centre-line dashes rather than three, because at 16 px three merge into a smear. The viewBox is 32 so the 16 px grid lands on whole units.
This note is a `desc` and not an XML comment for a reason worth knowing: the prose style of this repository uses a double hyphen, a double hyphen is illegal inside an XML comment, and an SVG that is not well-formed XML loads as an image of nothing -- `complete` true, `naturalWidth` 0, no error anywhere. Which is exactly how the first version of this file came out as a blank tab.
